# External-panel results of the intervention-transfer study (Gemma-2-2B; Wikipedia, six languages; written 2026-10-27 02:30 IST)

Produced ONCE by `scripts/g0/phase1_transfer_report.py` (code unchanged since commit `e99a457`, claim rules of amendment A14, 2,000 crossed-bootstrap replicates, seed 20261026) on the six validated external runs, after all six had been validated (last: `transfer-ext-feature-int16`, job 40546, 2026-10-27 02:26) and before any outcome statistic was read. The command (`<...>` = the directories under `/home/karma/Documents/ANLP/project/transfer_runs/`, outside git):

```
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 python scripts/g0/phase1_transfer_report.py --freeze reports/intervention_transfer/freeze.json --core reports/intervention_transfer/core_external.json \
  --cluster-mod 1000000 --group-languages eng_Latn spa_Latn rus_Cyrl zho_Hans hin_Deva yor_Latn --group-sentences 300 \
  --out <analysis_external> --feature-dir INT16=<transfer-ext-feature-int16> --feature-dir INT6=<transfer-ext-feature-int6> --feature-dir INT4=<transfer-ext-feature-int4> \
  --group-dir INT16=<transfer-ext-group-int16> --group-dir INT6=<transfer-ext-group-int6> --group-dir INT4=<transfer-ext-group-int4>
```

There is no `--survival` input (the Pearson survival file of the mask regime was computed on FLORES, not on this panel), so the survival question of the main study is not asked here and there is no `survival_validation.csv`. The cluster of an item is its passage (`--cluster-mod` above the number of passages: every passage its own cluster; no parallel translations).

Inputs: the output directories of Slurm jobs 40544, 40545, 40546 (feature level INT4, INT6, INT16; snapshot `repo_428f2ff`) and 40547, 40548, 40549 (group level INT4, INT6, INT16), with their sha256 in [`../../artifact_checksums.md`](../../artifact_checksums.md); the panel is `freeze_external.json` (wikimedia/wikipedia 20231101, revision `b04c8d1c…`, six languages, 300 evaluation passages each, 64 to 128 tokens; the text is only on Ada, CC BY-SA, not in git), the external core is [`../../core_external.json`](../../core_external.json) (402 of the 404 features, 6,406 feature-context pairs, 32,030 items per state; contexts chosen from full-precision activations only; amendments A11, A11b, A12). Files here: `claim_status.json`, `analysis_summary.json` (every number), `coverage.csv`, `component_summary.csv`, `specificity.csv`, `averaged_fingerprints.csv`, `averaged_features_<state>.csv`, `predictive_validation.csv`, `a3.csv`, `group_per_language.csv`; `figures/` (the four standard figures, light and dark, from `phase1_transfer_figures.py`). The per-item tables `per_context_<state>.csv` (26 MB each) stay outside git.

## Status of the pre-declared claims on the external panel (same rules as the main study; exploratory beyond them)

| claim | external panel | main study (for comparison) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 (context term of the fixed edit dominates the weight term, group level) | **mixed**: INT4 supported (median abs C 0.133, abs W 0.073, median difference +0.053 [+0.040, +0.064]; C larger in 4 of 6 languages), **INT6 reversed** (abs C 0.0076, abs W 0.0124, difference -0.0049 [-0.0060, -0.0031]; C larger in 2 of 6) | mixed: INT4 supported, INT6 undecided (difference -0.0008 [-0.0018, 0.0004]) |
| H1 (error is not a rescaling and not an activation change, and exceeds the floor) | **supported** at INT6 and INT4: error 1.77 [1.65, 1.97] and 7.07 [6.37, 7.87] floors; INT16 reference 0.76 [0.71, 0.80]; 97 to 99 % of the error is orthogonal to the FP effect (scalar residual share 0.992 INT6, 0.968 INT4); the quantized state's own activation leaves 98 to 100 % of it | supported (1.88 and 7.69 floors) |
| H2 (calibration and held-out agree; descriptive) | intervals overlap for C, W, I at both states | same |
| H3 (the generic sensitivity predicts the held-out error, 10 % rule) | **supported at both states**: INT4 19.4 % [5.1, 31.8] against A+G; INT6 23.4 % [12.8, 32.5] against A; INT16 reference 28.9 % [20.8, 37.0] | mixed: INT4 22.2 % supported, INT6 10.9 % [-1.2, 21.4] not |
| H4 (the averaged fingerprint transfers better than its contexts, beyond rounding) | **mixed**: INT4 supported (cosine gap +0.132 [0.125, 0.140] against the INT16 reference +0.027 [0.022, 0.033]), INT6 inconclusive (+0.039 [0.031, 0.044] overlaps the reference) | supported (INT4 +0.126, INT6 +0.024, reference +0.0145) |
| UTILITY (both states, 10 %) | **met** (INT4 19.4 %, INT6 23.4 %, interval of INT4 [5.1, 31.8] above zero but not above 10 %) | not met |

Eligible items: 200 of 402 features, 1,444 of 6,406 real items (22.5 %) clear five times the INT16 floor (main: 235 features, 2,203 items, 34.1 %); held-out half 659 items.

## Numbers behind the table

- **Group level (six languages x 300 passages x group + 3 controls; medians over the six languages; net harm).** Full-precision 0.182. INT6: 0.1666 (quantized context), 0.1887 (quantized weights), 0.1719 (both), 0.1809 (the state's own activation). INT4: 0.497, 0.2555, 0.774, native 0.310; terms abs C 0.133 [0.126, 0.143], abs W 0.073 [0.066, 0.081], median abs I 0.085; per language C larger in eng no, spa yes, rus yes, zho no, hin yes, yor yes. With the state's own activation the INT4 harm is 0.310 against 0.2555 with the quantized weights only (median per-language difference +0.0095); the medians over six languages are dominated by the heavy-tailed language zho_Hans (full-precision net harm 7.9), so they carry little weight.
- **Feature level (eligible real-direction items).** Cosine between the FP and the quantized effect vector 0.9975 (INT16), 0.982 (INT6), 0.754 (INT4); normalized error 0.064, 0.174, 0.679; norm ratio 1.00, 1.005, 1.088; relative terms at INT6 C 0.107, W 0.156, I 0.099; at INT4 C 0.352, W 0.579, I 0.340 (the weight term has the larger norm, as in the main study; the share of items with the C norm above the W norm is 0.066 at INT6 and 0.072 at INT4); interaction share of the change 0.386 and 0.363.
- **Specificity (real direction against its four controls; the controls are not eligibility-filtered).** INT4: normalized-error gap +0.023 [+0.014, +0.034], cosine gap +0.079 [+0.070, +0.089], the real direction's normalized error exceeds the mean of its four controls in 61 % of items; INT6: error gap -0.063 [-0.069, -0.058], cosine gap +0.033; INT16: -0.101, +0.024. Same pattern as the main study (INT4 +0.019 and +0.065): close to the controls in size, a little less rotated.
- **Averaged fingerprints (404 features).** The averaged fingerprint has the lower normalized error in 99.75 % of features at INT4 and INT6 and in all at INT16; cosine gaps above; coherence of the contexts of a feature in FP 0.54.
- **Prediction.** Eligible items, held-out error of A+B 0.0151 (INT16), 0.0294 (INT6), 0.1162 (INT4) against the null 0.0303, 0.0372, 0.1430; all-items secondary: reductions 33.3 % [27.3, 39.2] (INT16), 35.4 % [29.9, 40.5] (INT6), 21.2 % [15.2, 26.7] (INT4). The reduction in the rounding-only state (28.9 %) is as large as at INT4 and INT6, so the gain is not specific to quantization; the model measures how noise-prone a context is.

## Limits that must travel with every statement

Six languages and one corpus family, so this is an external-validity check and not a replication of the 27-language study (amendment A11, `not_claimed`); heavy-tailed group medians; 'held-out' means held-out FEATURES (the contexts of a held-out feature share passages with calibration contexts); the group-level interval covers passage sampling only and the H4 interval resamples features only; the numerical floor is large (bfloat16 execution) and was recomputed on this panel, so the eligible population differs from the main one (22.5 % against 34.1 %), which makes the INT6 statuses (A3 reversed, UTILITY met) less comparable to the main ones than the INT4 statuses; the INT16 reference is itself predicted by the same model (28.9 %), so UTILITY here does not show a quantization-specific mechanism; Chinese Traditional-character filtering of zho_Hans is a heuristic. The cross-corpus diagnostic declared in amendment A11 (E3; models fitted on the FLORES calibration features predict the external held-out items, no refit; a separate row, not part of the claim rules) is a separate step and is not in this directory yet.
